text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over many years, and people can live with it for a long time without noticing any signs. When early symptoms do appear, they are often mild.

list.snippet: Increased thirst and dry mouth: Higher blood sugar pulls fluids from your tissues, making you feel constantly thirsty.
Frequent urination: Your kidneys try to flush out extra blood sugar, which causes you to go to the bathroom more often, especially at night.
Persistent fatigue: Your cells cannot properly absorb glucose for energy, leaving you feeling tired and weak.
Blurred vision: Extra sugar in the blood can cause temporary swelling in the lens of the eye.
Slow-healing sores or cuts: High blood sugar impairs circulation and your immune system, making minor wounds take longer to heal.
Frequent infections: You may notice more recurring skin, gum, or urinary tract infections.
Tingling or numbness: Early nerve irritation (neuropathy) can cause a prickling sensation or numbness in your hands or feet.
Darkened skin patches: A condition called acanthosis nigricans causes dark, velvety patches to form in body folds like the neck, armpits, or groin.
Increased hunger: Despite eating, your body struggles to convert food into usable cellular energy.
